Automatic runner trace policies, video, native Linux, performance and release gates remain open.
scope: Public start/chunk/stop paths preserve phase names, original call/frame ownership, independent native clocks and immutable chunk boundaries.

Resource overflow and unsupported custom-element states preserve public action outcomes and prior output files; clean retirement permits a fresh recording. Full Chrome additionally verifies typed rejection of out-of-process snapshot frames.

Native admission bounds queued intents independently of full response bytes; evaluation/byte pressure waits under the original cancellation and deadline. Shared byte reservations survive archive failure and early ingestion until terminal transfer ownership settles.
retainedFailures: The initial public run exposed a failed network seal blocking retirement and a settled export rejection being stored as permanent cleanup failure. Both were corrected and have native/host regressions.

The first packed combined-artifact run exhausted worst-case bytes reserved by queued snapshot intents. Reply bytes are now reserved only at evaluation admission; queue limits remain unchanged.

A full-Chrome fixture assumed a remote frame already exposed its URL through the unsupported cross-process frame surface. The fixture now selects the actual child frame and verifies explicit remote snapshot rejection.
One test type error and one strict-lint test-module placement error were retained and corrected before the final passing batch.
